headline: Large User Grid Cost Responsibility
short_summary: This bill shifts the cost of grid infrastructure for large energy users, like data centers, away from residential ratepayers, aiming to prevent cost socialization.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor's office, environmental advocates.
opponents: Large energy users (data centers, hyperscalers like Meta, Google, Amazon, Microsoft), business lobbying groups.
news_headline: Virginia Weighs $1.5B Transmission Cost on Data Centers
news_summary: Virginia regulators are considering shifting approximately $1.5 billion in Dominion Energy transmission costs onto data center operators, with a decision expected by August 1, 2026. This aims to address concerns about residential ratepayers subsidizing infrastructure driven by data center demand.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates data centers to report their water consumption to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency regarding their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden/transparency concerns).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective January 1, 2027, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage to the Department of Environmental Quality, making this information publicly accessible. This aims to address concerns about the significant water consumption of data centers and provide better data for informed decisions.

headline: Data Center Siting & Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, homeowner associations, environmental groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry (due to increased regulatory burden).
news_headline: Virginia's New Data Center Law: What It Does, and What It Doesn't
news_summary: A new Virginia law, HB 153, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools and disclose utility infrastructure. While it mandates studies, it does not set specific noise limits or water caps, leaving some discretion to local authorities.
